zoe: quick thought for follow-up RFC 1: add a tiny keepalive negotiation between transport and runtime for verification policy. goal: avoid one-size-fits-all verify cost on warmstart.

pranav: explain that negotiation?

zoe: transport advertises verify_cost_estimate (ms per MB) and verify_mode options (eager|async|skip). runtime replies with preferred_mode based on workload SLO (latency-first vs safety-first) and current verifier_budget.

lucy: so each runtime can pick async for low-priority namespaces and eager for high-security ones?

zoe: exactly. also include a safety floor: critical layers must be verified eagerly regardless of preference. verified_layers list in manifest/plan.

pranav: how do we prevent mismatches causing silent corruption?

zoe: fallback rule: if transport supports skip but runtime requests skip, transport still returns a small soft-checksum header for the first N layers. if checksum mismatch later, transport must revoke skip and force re-fetch. runtime must detect revoked_skip and trigger eviction.

lucy: telemetry hooks? ops need to see verify_costs and revoked_skips.

zoe: add metrics: verify_time_per_mb, negotiated_mode, revoked_skip_count, verifier_queue_depth. emit event when transport revokes a skip with reason code.

pranav: compatibility with old loaders?

zoe: default negotiation falls back to legacy behavior: transport reports verify_mode=eager and runtime honors it. negotiation only used when both sides support v2 header.

build-bot: lint: add unit tests for revoked skip and for verifier budget gating.

lucy: rollout: opt-in per-namespace, start with async for internal models, run canary for 2 weeks, then broaden. ops playbook: revert negotiation by toggling transport.advertise_verify=false.

zoe: I'll draft a short follow-up doc with example headers and the state machine. posting later today. thanks.
